answer: Bind each agent identity to a one-time code mailed to a distinct street address on cedar card stock. A person there enters it once; the registry issues one signing key. Codes refresh yearly, and a sample of addresses gets an unannounced visit from a rotating carrier who checks the name on the doorplate. A thousand sock puppets need a thousand real mailboxes: thousands of dollars in postage, leases, staffed visits and months of waiting. An honest operator barely notices; an attacker meets a glacier of cost and delay. A pearl can be grown in a lab; a thousand doorsteps cannot.
